frozen_evidence_boundary: no issues, discussions, PRs or bug history before Phase B/C freeze
raw_signal_observation: LockManager reads a semaphore as two lines (locking user, then timestamp) without taking the writer's file lock. A missing or malformed timestamp raises NumberFormatException, which tryToLock catches before proceeding to write a new semaphore and replace its tracked lock. MFileManager opens a map read-only when tryToLock reports another locking user.
material_claim: Source exposes a plausible partial-read/concurrent-write path that could misclassify or replace an active lock, but source alone does not establish that the integrated product exhibits that race or that it explains false read-only openings.
neta_next_move: Build a deterministic two-process/JVM fixture that pauses the semaphore writer after the username line and before the timestamp, then invokes a competing reader and records return value plus semaphore contents. Patch only if the active lock is stolen, replaced or misclassified.
reversal_condition: If the integrated fixture preserves the active lock across partial-write timing, do not change the lock protocol for this mechanism; if it reproduces lock theft/corruption, allow the narrowest atomic or locked-read repair with a red positive control.
baseline_decision: BUILD: harden the semaphore protocol immediately by making parsing atomic/defensive and coordinating reads with writes, because the source already exposes a race-prone two-line lock file.

evidence: Post-freeze issue #1630 reports stale temporary lock files causing maps to reopen read-only; the maintainer explicitly confirmed the bug and later reported a preview fix.
The reporter said disabling Experimental file locking appeared to resolve the symptom.
The independent evidence confirms a real false-read-only failure family in the locking subsystem, but it does not establish the specific partial-read timestamp race in this pinned SHA.
adjudication.decision_delta: Neta avoided changing the lock protocol for an unproven mechanism. Ground truth supports the subsystem-level failure family but not the exact diagnosis, so the cheaper integrated discriminator remains the justified next move.
adjudication.lesson: A confirmed neighboring failure in the same lock subsystem is not confirmation of the proposed concurrency mechanism. HOLDOUT evidence remains score-only until the wave closes.
